rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should test a multimodal baseline to assess if combining RNA and image data improves performance. This configuration uses standard encoders (pca_n2000 for RNA, resnet50 for images) with simple concatenation fusion, isolating the effect of multimodal integration. It balances exploration of key design choices (model_setting=multimodal) while keeping other components minimal to avoid confounding factors.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat fusion) achieved 0.5266 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from 'concat' to 'weighted' improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It is the best next step as it directly compares two key multimodal design choices with minimal parameter changes, balancing exploration of fusion methods and exploitation of the existing multimodal framework.

The existing evidence shows multimodal singleprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieve ~0.52 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile (a key design choice) with the same encoders but avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile setting. It balances exploration of multiprofile (which may capture more cell heterogeneity) while reusing proven components, reducing uncertainty about profile setting's impact.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion achieve high accuracy (0.6186). This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (instead of concat) improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It builds on the promising multiprofile foundation while exploring a critical design choice with minimal parameter changes.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.639). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l, a more advanced vision transformer, while keeping the proven aggregation and fusion settings. This clarifies whether a stronger image encoder can further improve performance, balancing exploration of image modality improvements with exploitation of existing effective configurations.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.639). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation in the same setup, isolating the impact of aggregation method. Transformer aggregation could capture more complex interactions between modalities, and this comparison directly addresses a key design choice with potential for improvement.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile models with weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether switching from avgpool to transformer aggregation (while keeping weighted fusion) further improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It is the best use of the remaining budget as it directly builds on the current top-performing configuration with minimal changes.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile models with pca_n2000 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.639). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping other components the same, to isolate the effect of aggregation method. This is a critical design choice with potential to improve performance, and aligns with the budget to exploit promising directions.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA encoder, and avgpool aggregation achieve high accuracy (0.638999 in config_019). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation using the same pca_n2000 and imagenet_vit_l encoders, to determine if transformer aggregation could further improve performance. This clarifies the impact of aggregation method on model performance, a critical design choice with potential for significant gains.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.639). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 in this top-performing setup to isolate the impact of RNA representation. It balances exploitation of the multiprofile/weighted fusion pattern with exploration of a different RNA encoder, which could potentially improve performance without changing other critical design choices.
